revisionDesc.change: Vote - AcceptText - MZR is right about Ἁρυώτῃ in line 1. There is no iota adscript (Sosin appears to have been looking at Ἁρυώτου at the very end of the line). I am willing to accept Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος) in line 9. As an iota it is slightly more curved than, e.g., that at the end of πρόκειται in ln. 10, but as Sosin points out comparison with PSI 8.916.10 encourages adopting Ταορσεῦτι. Lin1 subscr τεσσεράκοντα is fine.

Vote - AcceptText - Accept. Lin1: I am not fully persuaded by Ἁρυώτηι → Ἁρυώτῃ ; it is the end of the line and the papyrus is slightly damaged; I could not swear that there is no iota there. Lin9 Ταορσεῦτ<ο>ς → Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος) seems a bit of a coin-toss to me. The iota would be more curved than the others in m2; but the sigma would be less round than the others in m2. But PSI VIII 916.10 also reads (new reading my Zellmann-Rohrer) Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος), which supports Ταορσεῦτι. So, I am inclined to accept. Lin1 subscr τεσσεράκοντα is clear.

line 1: Ἁρυώτηι → Ἁρυώτῃ based on digital image (Michigan APIS): the adscript is not present line 9: Ταορσεῦτ<ο>ς → Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος) based on the digital image. Sigma in this hand has a more pronounced curvature; iota can be slightly curved, as in the second iota in πρόκειται (line 10) subscriptions, line 1: τεσσαράκοντα → τεσσεράκοντα based on digital image
